elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The licence extends only to affiliates identified in a written notice to Contractor, rather than to all Company affiliates automatically.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: No operative language extends the licence to contractors acting on Company's behalf.
The operative licence is expressly perpetual.
The licence is not stated to be irrevocable; perpetual duration alone does not establish irrevocability.

elements.element: Any subscription licence may be terminated only for an uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: No subscription licence is granted in the provided operative language; the stated licence is perpetual, so the condition is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Transferability is limited to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction and therefore does not cover successors generally.

elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates identified in a written notice.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence expressly extends the licence to any Company affiliate identified in a written notice to Contractor.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence expressly permits transfer to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction without Contractor's approval.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the two fallback requirements but not the broader preferred position. It adds only the affiliate-notice extension and M&A-successor transfer right, with the no-approval language appropriately addressing the consent restriction in Section 10. Unrelated commercial terms remain operative, although an express 'notwithstanding Section 10' formulation would make the transfer carve-out clearer.
